Let
\[
m_j=\int z^j\,d\mu(z),\qquad m_0=1,\qquad m_1=\rho,\qquad m_2=\cdots=m_{r-1}=0,
\]
and write \(m_r=w\).

Consider the Toeplitz moment matrix
\[
T=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\rho&0&\cdots&0&\overline w\\
\rho&1&\rho&\cdots&0&0\\
0&\rho&1&\ddots&0&0\\
\vdots&&\ddots&\ddots&\rho&\vdots\\
0&0&0&\rho&1&\rho\\
w&0&0&\cdots&\rho&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Every representing measure gives \(T\succeq0\). Conversely, by the finite Toeplitz moment theorem, every such positive semidefinite matrix is represented by a probability measure on the unit circle.

Let \(A\) be the upper-left \(r\times r\) principal block. Its determinant is \(D_r\), and the hypothesis on \(\rho\) implies \(A\succ0\). The relevant entries of \(A^{-1}\) are
\[
(A^{-1})_{00}=(A^{-1})_{r-1,r-1}=\frac{D_{r-1}}{D_r},
\qquad
(A^{-1})_{0,r-1}=\frac{(-\rho)^{r-1}}{D_r}.
\]

Writing \(x=\operatorname{Re}w\), the Schur complement condition \(T\succeq0\) becomes
\[
D_{r-1}|w|^2+2(-1)^{r-1}\rho^r x+D_{r-1}\rho^2\le D_r.
\]
For fixed \(x\), the left side is minimized when \(w=x\) is real. Hence the maximal \(x\) is the larger root of
\[
D_{r-1}x^2+2(-1)^{r-1}\rho^r x+D_{r-1}\rho^2-D_r=0.
\]

Using
\[
D_n^2-D_{n-1}D_{n+1}=\rho^{2n},
\]
the discriminant simplifies to \(D_r^2\). Therefore
\[
\max \operatorname{Re}m_r
=
\frac{D_r-(-1)^{r-1}\rho^r}{D_{r-1}}.
\]

At the maximum, \(w\) is real and \(T\) has rank \(r\). Thus every maximizing measure has exactly \(r\) support points.

To compute their sum, let \(v=(v_0,\dots,v_r)^T\) span \(\ker T\), normalized by \(v_r=1\). Then
\[
(v_0,\dots,v_{r-1})^T=-A^{-1}(x,0,\dots,0,\rho)^T,
\]
so
\[
v_{r-1}
=
-\frac{(-\rho)^{r-1}x+\rho D_{r-1}}{D_r}.
\]
The associated degree-\(r\) polynomial vanishes at the conjugates of the support points, so by Vieta,
\[
\sum_{\zeta\in\operatorname{supp}\mu}\zeta
=
-v_{r-1}
=
\frac{(-\rho)^{r-1}x+\rho D_{r-1}}{D_r}.
\]
Substituting the value of \(x\) gives the requested triple:
\[
\boxed{
\left(
\frac{D_r-(-1)^{r-1}\rho^r}{D_{r-1}},
\quad
r,
\quad
\frac{\rho D_{r-1}^2+(-\rho)^{r-1}\bigl(D_r-(-1)^{r-1}\rho^r\bigr)}
{D_{r-1}D_r}
\right)
}.
\]
